decision_conditions: The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Energy Statement prepared by NRG Consulting, dated November 2024 unless otherwise submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved measures for reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, including but not limited to the use of low and zero carbon technologies, enhanced building fabric performance, and energy-efficient systems, shall be fully implemented prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafter.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development shall be designed and constructed to ensure that the internal consumption of potable water does not exceed 105 litres per person per day. This shall be achieved through the installation of water-efficient fittings, appliances, and, where applicable, water recycling systems. The development shall be maintained in accordance with these measures for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD58 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/Reasons: In the interests of good air quality with regard to London Plan policies 5.3 and 7.14

Prior to above ground works, details of ecological enhancements including, but not limited to, bat bricks/tiles and bird bricks/tubes/boxes to be used in the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Confirmation of installation, , together with accompanying photographic evidence shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority prior to first occupationReason: To enhance the site post development in line with Core Policy 36 by providing suitable nesting features for birds and bats.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including site clearance and all preparatory work) a full tree survey in accordance with BS5837:2012 shall be completed by a professional arboriculturist and submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include a finalized tree retention/removal plan, arboricultural impact assessment and tree constraints plan.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees on and adjacent to the site have been sufficiently assessed and considered, in their condition and quality, and in their relation to the development, in accordance with DMD 80 and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Notwithstanding the submitted plans, prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved, whichever is the sooner; full details of all proposed tree planting shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include:a)	Planting and aftercare specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of locations;b)	species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times;c)	tree pit design (where appropriate) and;d)	underground modular systems (where appropriate).Planting and aftercare specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of locations; species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier and defect period. All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times; tree pit design (where appropriate) and; underground modular systems (where appropriate).Reason: To ensure that the aesthetic and ecological value of the site is enhanced post development in line with the Biodiversity Action Plan, Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and the Publication London Plan.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995 or any amending Order, no buildings or extensions to buildings shall be erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure adherence to the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 1995.

The development shall not be occupied until details of a minimum of 8 secure and covered cycle parking spaces for the development have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, meeting the requirements of the London Cycle Design Standards. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before it is occupied.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), the Council's adopted standards and London Cycling Design Standards Chapter 8

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including site clearance and all preparatory work) a scheme for the protection of all retained trees in accordance with BS5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall comprise an Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS), and Tree Protection Plans (TPP). The development shall be carried out in full compliance with the Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plans unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plans shall contain: full details of all aspects of design, site clearance, and construction work with the potential to affect trees, physical measures for the protection of trees, and construction practices, site management and if applicable arboricultural supervision to demonstrate how retained trees will be adequately protected. Plans shall be of legible scale, dimensioned where appropriate. The AMS and TPPs shall include the following information:o	Provide the siting and design of all aspects of works within the Root Protection Area (RPA), or which otherwise have the potential to affect retained trees, to demonstrate how all aspects of design will prevent damage to trees:o	Location and installation of all drainage and utility services including temporary serviceso	Full specification for the construction of hard surfacing including existing and proposed ground levels. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) the specification / plan shall demonstrate how it will be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses.o	Details of all other hard and soft landscaping within RPAs of retained trees.o	Location and installation of buildings, boundary treatments and ancillary structures, in or close to RPAs.o	Location and specification of any remediation works.o	Existing and proposed ground levels.o	Identify different phases of the works for which a different arrangement of tree protection will be required. For each phase, prepare a Tree Protection Plan to show the following:-	Location of retained trees (and their post pruning crown spread if applicable).-	Location of Construction Exclusion Zones.-	Location of tree protective fencing.-	Location of ground protection.-	Location of all works to be undertaken during that phase and construction space for their implementation.-	Location of site access, parking, loading, unloading, welfare facilities and storage of equipment, materials, fuels, mixing of concrete, applicable to that phase.-	Provide specification for tree works, protective fencing and ground protection.-	Identify site preparation and construction practices and site management arrangements to prevent damage to trees. Aspects to include: clearance of vegetation, erection and installation of: buildings and structures, hard surfacing, drainage and utilities, boundary treatments, remediation works, planting, and all other demolition and construction activities.Reason: To protect important landscape features within the site in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved refuse storage details as set out in  drawing NWA-23-011-1 before the development is occupied. The refuse storage shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the developmentReason: To ensure the provision of refuse storage in accordance with the London Borough of Enfield - Waste and Recycling Planning Storage Guidance ENV 08/162.

Prior to above ground works full details of the proposed fire hydrant as submitted in drawing NWA-23-011-1 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation of the development and permanently retained.Reason: In the interest of fire safety and emergency servicing.

No development other than ground works, site clearance or other enabling works shall take place until a Biodiversity Net Gain Plan (BNG) scheme has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.The scheme shall: o	Show how at least 10% measurable BNG will be achieved in line with the Environment Act 2021o	Indentify where and how the BNG will be deliveredo	Include any legal or financial measures needed to be secure its delivery. Reason: To ensure the development achieves measurable biodiversity net gain in accordance with the Environment Act 2021.

The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, as set out in the attached schedule which forms part of this notice.NWA-23-011-1NWA-23-011-2NWA-23-011-3NWA-23-011-LOC_PNWA-23-011-LOC_EEnergy StatementBNG StatementBNG AssessmentDesign & Access StatementFlood Risk Assessment Tree SurveyEcological SurveyTopographical Survey Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Prior to above ground works, a schedule specifying all external materials to be used including details of the proposed front fence as well as samples and detailed drawings (at 1:20 and 1:5) including: brickwork (bespoke 1m x 1m sample panel constructed on site for officer review in person - inc. bond, joint and mortar); brick detailing; party wall parapets and roof edge, eaves and ridge junctions; window and door openings and installations including frame and window bars (minimum reveal depth 1 brick / 215mm); bay window and porch canopy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. This schedule may, for example, include written details of manufacturer, product name or number (if applicable) and surface colour/texture together with precedent imagery at varying scales. Reason: To ensure that the finished appearance of the development will respect the character and visual amenities of the local area.

The development shall not commence until a Sustainable Drainage Strategy has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  The details shall be based on the disposal of surface water by means of a sustainable drainage system in accordance with the principles as set out in the Technical Guidance to the National Planning Policy Framework and should be in line with our DMD Policy SuDS Requirements:a)	Shall be designed to a 1 in 1 and 1 in 100 year storm event with the allowance for climate changeb)	Follow the London Plan Drainage Hierarchy and providing evidence of the potential for full infiltration SuDS and maximising above ground storagec)	Follow the SuDS management train by providing source control for the site, and a number of treatment phases corresponding to their pollution potential d)	Maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation valuee)	The system must be designed to allow for flows that exceed the design capacity to be stored on site or conveyed off-site with minimum impactf)	Clear ownership, management and maintenance arrangements must be establishedg)	The details submitted shall include levels, sizing, cross sections and specifications for all drainage featuresReason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value

The development shall not commence until a Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Management Plan shall be written in accordance with London Best Practice Guidance and contain:o	A photographic condition survey of the public roads, footways and verges leading to the site;o	Details of construction access and associated traffic management;o	Arrangements for the loading, unloading and turning of delivery, construction and service vehicles;o	Arrangements for the parking of contractors' vehicles;o	Arrangements for wheel cleaning;o	Arrangements for the storage of materials;o	Hours of work;o	The storage and removal of excavation material;o	Measures to reduce danger to cyclists;o	Dust mitigation measures;o	Membership of the Considerate Contractors SchemeThe development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Construction Management Plan unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure construction does not lead to damage of the nearby public road network and to minimise disruption to the neighbouring properties.

No development shall take place until Construction Management Plan, written in accordance with the Mayor of London's supplementary planning guidance 'The Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' detailing how dust and emissions will be managed during demolition and construction work shall be submitted to the local planning authority for approval. Once approved the Construction Management Plan shall be fully implemented for the duration of any demolition and construction works.Reason: To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.
